```json
  "id": "roshan-bay-veil-open",
  "name": "Roshan Bay Open",
  "verb": "filter through",
  "idea": "A modal opens from one centred bay a third of its width, the roshan's one open part to two plain, and widens to full on a single decelerating curve with true rounded corners, while a light blur clears by 70% so the content is sharp before the open lands.",
  "use": [
    "modal",
    "sheet"
  ],
  "trigger": "enter",
  "target": "self",
  "stagger": 0,
  "origin": "50% 50%",
  "keyframes": [
    {
      "offset": 0,
      "easing": "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.75, 0.55, 0.9)",
      "opacity": 0,
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 33.33% 0% 33.33% round 16px)",
      "filter": "blur(4px)"
    },
    {
      "offset": 0.35,
      "easing": "cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.3, 0.7, 0.9)",
      "opacity": 1,
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 9% 0% 9% round 16px)",
      "filter": "blur(1.5px)"
    },
    {
      "offset": 0.7,
      "easing": "cubic-bezier(0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 1)",
      "opacity": 1,
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 1.5% 0% 1.5% round 16px)",
      "filter": "blur(0px)"
    },
    {
      "offset": 1,
      "opacity": 1,
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 0% 0% 0% round 16px)",
      "filter": "blur(0px)"
    }
  ],
  "timing": {
    "duration": 380,
    "delay": 0,
    "easing": "linear",
    "iterations": 1,
    "direction": "normal",
    "fill": "both"
  },
  "reduced": {
    "kind": "fade",
    "ms": 200,
    "note": "The modal fades in at full width with its rounded corners, with no opening and no blur."
  },
  "cardIds": [
    "hejazi-rawashin-windows"
  ],
  "lensIds": [
    "hejazi-roshan"
  ],
  "culturalNotes": "Follows the roshan, plural rawasheen, the projecting wooden window bays whose turned and carved lattice panels were made by Hejazi builders and carpenters for the old houses of Al-Balad in Historic Jeddah, a UNESCO World Heritage site. The motion borrows the lens's proportion of about one part open bay to two parts plain wall. The panel starts as one narrow centred bay a third of its width and opens evenly to both sides, so it reads the same in right-to-left and left-to-right layouts. The light blur that clears early borrows the way the lattice lets light through while screening what is behind. It draws no carving, no lattice picture, no text and no real facade."

```

The mismatch came from the curve on the whole run. In WAAPI, timing.easing bends the full 0 to 1 run, but in CSS the same curve is applied to each keyframe segment, so with four keyframes the two drifted apart at the first sample.

What changed:
- timing.easing is now "linear".
- The decelerating feel now lives in each keyframe's own easing, so CSS and WAAPI play the same frames.
- The middle values were re-sampled from the old overall curve so it still reads as one decelerating open:
  - inset 9% and blur 1.5px at 35%
  - inset 1.5% and sharp at 70%
  - full at the end
- Each segment's curve is tuned so its end speed matches the next segment's start speed. This avoids any visible stall at the joins.

The id, idea, ties, proportions, blur clearing by 70%, reduced fallback and cultural notes are unchanged.
